years_since_diagnosis.evidence: Crohn's hit me like a truck two years ago.

occupation.evidence: Software engineer, thankfully can work remotely when needed.

severity.evidence: CT showed massive inflammation. Emergency colonoscopy confirmed severe Crohn's. GI says my disease aggressive.

disease_control.evidence: Humira/methotrexate combination helping more than Humira alone but only ~60% improvement; surgery looming; disease described as aggressive; living scan to scan.

treatments.reason_stopped: Inpatient course; transitioned to oral prednisone
treatments.evidence: Started IV steroids immediately. Spent week in hospital.

treatments.reason_stopped: Tapered off; caused steroid-induced diabetes and osteoporosis
treatments.evidence: High-dose prednisone for two months. Developed steroid-induced diabetes. Tapered prednisone.
Tapered prednisone, started azathioprine. Helped minimally.

treatments.reason_stopped: Developed antibodies after about a year; stopped working
treatments.evidence: Started Remicade... Remicade worked initially... But after year, developed antibodies. Stopped working.
Switched to Humira. The every two week injection manageable but not as effective as Remicade was. Maybe 60% improvement.
Doctor added methotrexate. Nausea terrible first few months. Hair thinning. But combination helping more than Humira alone.

encounters.evidence: Emergency room visit started everything. Severe pain, bloody diarrhea, fever. CT showed massive inflammation. Emergency colonoscopy confirmed severe Crohn's. Started IV steroids immediately. Spent week in hospital.

GI pushed for biologics quickly given severity. Started Remicade... Switched to Humira... Doctor added methotrexate. Next step if Humira/methotrexate combo fails is Stelara or Entyvio. GI says my disease aggressive.

status.evidence: Switched to Humira. The every two week injection manageable but not as effective as Remicade was.

barriers.evidence: Insurance company from hell. Denied coverage three times. Meanwhile, I'm deteriorating. Lawyer helped appeal. Finally approved after four months.

referral_steps_gp_to_prescriber.evidence: Patient went directly to ER where Crohn's was diagnosed and IV steroids started; GI specialist then managed ongoing treatment including biologics. No GP/PCP step mentioned. ER -> GI = 1 step to prescriber.

extraction_notes: Calcium, vitamin D, and bisphosphonates excluded from treatments as they treat steroid-induced osteoporosis (a comorbidity), not Crohn's directly. Insulin excluded as it treats steroid-induced diabetes comorbidity. Stelara and Entyvio mentioned as future contingency options only ('next step if combo fails') — not yet started or formally planned, so not added to treatments. Remicade was the first biologic (now stopped); Humira is the current biologic. The biologic_decision_point is placed at the GI encounter where Remicade was first prescribed and all subsequent biologic decisions occurred. No GP/PCP encounter mentioned; patient went directly to ER.
